title: Saved network connections
whyItMatters: NetworkManager stores every saved Wi-Fi, VPN and mobile connection here, including Wi-Fi passwords and often VPN credentials in plain text. It maps the networks the person used and can give a stranger access to them.
source: NetworkManager.conf(5): system-connections names the directory of connection profiles, default /etc/NetworkManager/system-connections: https://networkmanager.dev/docs/api/latest/NetworkManager.conf.html
notes: The keyfiles are normally mode 600 and owned by root, so a normal user cannot list or read them; the engine records the skip instead of failing. Wi-Fi passphrases and some VPN secrets are stored in clear text in these files when they are not held by a secret agent, which is why the rule is critical.

steps: Open Settings > Wi-Fi and use the menu next to each saved network to forget it.
For VPN profiles use Settings > Network > VPN. An administrator password may be required.
Leave any system profiles that Settings does not list to the full reset at the end of this plan.
cleanup.risk: Removes the saved Wi-Fi passphrases and VPN profiles that Settings lists. You will need to enter those network passwords again. Profiles saved for other users stay until the full reset at the end of the plan.
cleanup.source: GNOME Help, Connect to a wireless network: https://help.gnome.org/users/gnome-help/stable/net-wireless-connect.html
